payload.claim: commit_squash and render_pr_body (line 770) are still handed the run's `base_sha`, never `target_head`/`tree_base`, so the squash commit's own message ('base {base_sha[:12]}') and the PR body's Provenance section ('base `{base_sha}`') will name a commit that is not the tree the patch was actually applied onto. This diff updates every other consumer of the applied base (assert_base_objects, apply target, diff_stat, needs_reverification, the conflict/new-failure watch strings, --base) to use target_head/tree_base, but misses these two — and the new stacked-package test proves the authors knew base_sha and tree_base diverge (it deliberately sets base_sha to 40 zeros as a decoy) yet never asserts on the commit message or the Provenance line, so nothing catches that a real stacked PR (once SA-0026 passes parent_branch) will push a commit whose own message records a base that is not its git parent — a permanent, unfixable-after-the-fact misstatement in a persisted artifact.
